question: Will the official result of the Lamag by-election (Sabah), scheduled for January 24, 2026, be overturned before May 1, 2026?
summary: Objections correctly identify nonzero overturn risk due to ongoing Sabah election petitions (Sindumin, Pintasan) and broader petition activity, which is a genuine blind spot in assuming stability solely from Lamag's margin.
The threshold analysis and public reporting show a large Lamag margin (5,681) and no Lamag overturn reported by May 1, 2026, supporting a low base rate but not a zero probability.
Procedural hurdles and past Sabah petitions (e.g., Bengkoka) suggest overturns are difficult, reinforcing caution but not eliminating risk.
Overall, the ensemble probability is kept but nudged upward modestly to reflect real but small overturn risk, resulting in a calibrated interval.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid in signaling a nonzero risk from petitions but do not reveal a systematic error in the ensemble; the adjustment is modest and conservative.
justification.adjustment: Raised from 0.02 to 0.04 to acknowledge nonzero petition-driven risk; the range 0.02–0.08 captures remaining uncertainty. No downward adjustment was warranted given the procedural barriers and lack of Lamag-specific overturns reported by May 1, 2026.

causal-factors.name: Large Lamag margin reduces likelihood of overturn
causal-factors.rationale: The Lamag result shows a decisive majority (7,269–1,588, margin 5,681), which tends to make successful petition overturns less likely than in close races. (Sources: Malay Mail, turn0search1; Wikipedia, turn0search12)

causal-factors.name: Active Sabah election petitions in other seats raise nonzero overturn risk
causal-factors.rationale: Petitions have been filed for Pintasan and Sindumin, indicating ongoing legal challenges to Sabah election results that could set precedents or influence judicial scrutiny. (Sources: The Star, turn1search0; The Borneo Post, turn1search7)

causal-factors.name: Bengkoka petition struck out demonstrates procedural barriers to overturns
causal-factors.rationale: The election court struck out the Bengkoka petition on preliminary grounds, illustrating high procedural hurdles for reversing results. (Source: New Straits Times, turn0search3)

causal-factors.name: No Lamag-specific overturn reported by May 1, 2026 despite petitions elsewhere
causal-factors.rationale: Official Lamag results were announced January 24, 2026 and, as of May 1, 2026, there were no verified reversals reported. (Sources: Malay Mail, turn0search1; The Vibes, turn0search2)

causal-factors.name: Lack of publicly reported Lamag-specific irregularities reduces grounds for reversal
causal-factors.rationale: Unlike Sindumin, Lamag has not generated widely publicized irregularities that would support voiding the result; petitions so far focus on other seats. (Sources: The Star on Pintasan petition, turn1search0; The Borneo Post on Sindumin petitions, turn0search4)

causal-factors.name: Large Lamag margin (5,681 votes)
causal-factors.rationale: Lamag was won by BN with a 5,681-vote majority (7,269 to 1,588), announced January 24, 2026, and the winner was sworn in later, which substantially raises the bar for overturning the result via petition. (Sources cited include The Star live coverage and Malay Mail confirmation; further context in the general reporting of the by-elections.)

causal-factors.name: Ongoing Sabah election petitions (Sindumin, Pintasan, etc.)
causal-factors.rationale: Sabah has active petitions challenging several seats, including Sindumin and Pintasan, and even independent challenges have been aired, which keeps the possibility of overturn alive despite Lamag's large margin. (Sources cited include Malay Mail on Sindumin petition, Sabah-centric reporting, and related Sabah petition coverage.)

causal-factors.name: Recent court action upholding BN wins in Sabah (Bengkoka petition struck out)
causal-factors.rationale: The Election Court struck out the Bengkoka petition, with BN’s win upheld, which lowers the odds that Sabah election petitions will overturn results, including Lamag. (Source: NST reporting on the Bengkoka petition outcome.)

causal-factors.name: Unity-government framing of Lamag results
causal-factors.rationale: Media framing the Lamag result as a sign of unity government strength may dampen incentives to pursue overturns, contributing a downstream pressure against reversal. (Source: The Star coverage describing Lamag/Lamag context as a unity-government signal.)

causal-factors.name: Lamag margin (5,681 votes) provides a strong barrier to overturn
causal-factors.rationale: The Lamag result showed 7,269 votes for BN vs 1,588 for Warisan, a margin of 5,681, making a successful petition overturn unlikely; official results were announced January 24, 2026 and the winner sworn in February 10, 2026. ([malaymail.com](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2026/01/24/bn-retains-lamag-seat-mohd-ismail-wins-with-majority-of-5681-kinabatangan-result-still-unofficial/206706?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Active Sabah election petitions in Sindumin and Pintasan raise nonzero overturn risk
causal-factors.rationale: Petitions filed or pursued in Sindumin and Pintasan (with preliminary objections in Sindumin as of January 29, 2026) indicate ongoing challenges to Sabah election results, which could theoretically affect Lamag via legal precedent; no Lamag overturn reported by May 1, 2026. ([thestar.com.my](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/01/08/warisan-challenges-sabah-election-results?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Procedural hurdles and prior Sabah petition outcomes favor dismissal of challenges
causal-factors.rationale: Sabah election petitions such as Bengkoka have been struck out on procedural grounds, underscoring high legal hurdles for overturns; this lowers the likelihood of Lamag being overturned by May 1, 2026. ([nst.com.my](https://www.nst.com.my/amp/news/regional/2026/02/1383883/bns-harun-durabi-keeps-bengkoka-seat-election-court-strikes-out?utm_source=openai))

synthesis: Lamag's strong margin reduces overturn likelihood, but active Sabah petitions keep a nonzero risk. The ensemble base is adjusted modestly upward to reflect this nonzero risk, while still acknowledging significant barriers to reversal.
